senses.sense_definition: A large sheet of muscle separating the chest from the abdomen that contracts and relaxes to aid in breathing.

examples.text: Singers often learn to control their breathing by using the <w>diaphragm</w>.
The doctor explained that hiccups occur when your <w>diaphragm</w> spasms suddenly.

senses.sense_definition: A dome-shaped silicone or rubber contraceptive cup that covers the cervix to prevent pregnancy.

examples.text: She spoke with her gynecologist to determine if a <w>diaphragm</w> was a suitable birth control method.
The patient was instructed on how to insert and remove the <w>diaphragm</w> correctly.

senses.sense_definition: A device or partition with an adjustable aperture used to regulate the amount of light entering an optical system such as a camera.

examples.text: Adjusting the camera's <w>diaphragm</w> changes the amount of light that hits the sensor.
The photographer widened the <w>diaphragm</w> to create a shallow depth of field.

senses.sense_definition: A thin, vibrating membrane in a speaker, microphone, or telephone receiver that converts sound waves to or from electrical signals.

examples.text: Sound waves hit the thin <w>diaphragm</w> inside the microphone and create an electrical signal.
The high volume caused the speaker's delicate <w>diaphragm</w> to tear.

senses.sense_definition: Any biological membrane, ligament, or muscular partition separating anatomical cavities.

examples.text: The pelvic <w>diaphragm</w> provides crucial support to the internal organs of the pelvis.
Surgeons carefully inspected the muscular <w>diaphragm</w> during the abdominal operation.

senses.sense_definition: A flexible dividing membrane in a mechanical chamber or valve that flexes in response to differences in fluid pressure.

examples.text: A rupture in the pressure regulator's <w>diaphragm</w> caused the entire hydraulic system to fail.
The pump utilizes a flexible rubber <w>diaphragm</w> to draw liquid into the chamber.

senses.sense_definition: A porous or semipermeable dividing layer used in an electrolytic cell or chemical apparatus.

examples.text: In the chlor-alkali process, an asbestos <w>diaphragm</w> keeps the chlorine separate from the hydroxide solution.
Ions migrate through the porous <w>diaphragm</w> as the electrical current flows.

senses.sense_definition: A structural element, such as a floor slab or roof panel, that resists and transfers lateral forces to vertical structural members.

examples.text: Engineers designed the concrete floor slab to act as a rigid <w>diaphragm</w> during an earthquake.
Wind loads are transmitted horizontally through the roof <w>diaphragm</w> to the shear walls.

senses.sense_definition: To reduce the aperture of an optical system or lens.

examples.text: The astronomer <w>diaphragmed</w> down the lens to reduce distortion while observing the bright planet.
Before taking the exposure, the technician <w>diaphragmed</w> the optical device to control light levels.

senses.sense_definition: To vibrate or behave like a mechanical diaphragm.

examples.text: Engineers discovered that the metal cover was <w>diaphragming</w> intensely at high rotational speeds.
Excessive acoustic pressure caused the thin plate to <w>diaphragm</w> and generate unwanted noise.
